title: Can catering companies in Dubai provide serving staff and cleanup?
meta_title: Catering Staff and Cleanup: What to Confirm | myCHEF
meta_description: Serving staff and cleanup can be part of a Dubai catering booking when written into the scope. A role list, cleanup table and handover checklist.
excerpt: What to confirm about servers, washing-up and the final handover before you book catering for a Dubai home or venue.
body_html:
Yes. Catering companies in Dubai can provide serving staff and post-event cleanup, but neither is automatic from the phrase 'full service'. Both need to be written into the proposal: who serves, until what time, and which areas are cleaned. When you enquire through our Dubai catering team, list the serving and cleanup tasks you want covered so the proposal can answer them directly.

What serving staff actually cover

Ask for responsibilities by role rather than a total headcount. A cook finishing dishes in the kitchen and a server attending the table are different jobs, and neither necessarily covers drinks, furniture or waste removal.

  • Setup: placing agreed serving equipment and preparing the food area.
  • Service: bringing dishes to the table, attending a buffet or circulating canapés.
  • Replenishment: keeping the agreed food presentation ready during service.
  • Dietary questions: identifying dishes and passing dietary questions to the right person.
  • Clearing: removing used plates, serving dishes and agreed glassware.
  • Supervision: coordinating the team and handling changes with your nominated contact.

Cleanup: what it includes and excludes

'Cleanup included' means different things to different providers. The useful version is a task list with an area list beside it:

Area or taskAsk the caterer to confirmDo not assume
Preparation areaCatering utensils washed, surfaces wipedHousehold appliances or existing mess
Dining areaCatering crockery and food items clearedFurniture moved or decorations removed
Washing-upWhich dishes are washed, and whereHousehold and hired items treated alike
WasteBagged and moved to an agreed pointAll event rubbish removed from the property
Hired equipmentPacked, stored and collection agreedCollection happens the same evening

Agree the handover as its own stage

Set separate milestones for setup, guest service, clearing and handover, and nominate one person to check the agreed areas before the team leaves. Also ask what happens if the evening runs past the agreed service window, and who can authorise an extension.

A worked example (hypothetical)

A host books a plated dinner for eighteen in a villa garden. The written scope names two service staff until 23:00, plated courses with one vegetarian alternative identified per guest, clearing of the dining table and garden buffet, washing-up of catering items only, and bagged waste taken to the service gate. Hired platters are packed for collection the next morning and stored in the garage. Everything not on that list — bar glassware, cushions, the pool area — stays with the household. The example is illustrative; it shows how a scope reads when it is specific, not a recorded booking.

Questions to send with your enquiry

  • Which roles are included: cook, servers, wash-up, supervision?
  • What are the service start and finish times, and how are extensions handled?
  • Exactly which cleanup tasks and areas are covered?
  • Where does bagged waste go, and when is equipment collected?
  • How are dietary requirements identified at the table?

For event catering that lists its inclusions clearly, start with our catering page, then use the guide to comparing catering quotes in Dubai.
